findings.title: Possible nil pointer dereference on photodiode config
findings.message: The new condition dereferences p.Device.Photo without nil checks. Other code paths, such as photodiodeControls, guard against p.Device == nil || p.Device.Photo == nil. Any photodiode component lacking a populated Photo config, for example from a partially decoded or legacy document, would panic inside the solver.
findings.suggestion: Guard the dereference: `p.Kind == "photodiode" && p.Device != nil && p.Device.Photo != nil && p.Device.Photo.Capacitance > 0`. Wrap the photodiode term in parentheses for clarity.

findings.title: Variable shadows builtin copy
findings.message: The local variable `copy` shadows Go's builtin copy function, which hurts readability and can confuse later edits.

findings.title: Unsynchronized access to service internals and unchecked lookup
findings.message: The test reads the service's internal `s.graph` directly while the service may be running worker goroutines, which can race under -race. The test also ignores the existence flag, so a missing component causes a nil-pointer panic instead of a clear failure. The same flag is ignored for `old, _ :=` above.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the component from a published snapshot after `settled(t, s)` rather than reading the internal `s.graph`. If no such snapshot accessor exists, read `s.graph` only under the service's synchronization. Check the `exists` result and nil-check `Device`/`Photo` before dereferencing.
